Keeping your hips elevated, slowly slide both heels outward along the floor, allowing your legs to extend and your hips to lower in a controlled descent.
Keeping your hips elevated, slowly slide your working heel toward your glutes by bending the knee. Continue until your knee is bent to roughly 90 degrees or as far as your flexibility allows.
Keeping your hips facing forward and feet planted, slowly rotate your torso and arms to one side through a large, controlled arc.
Keeping your hips grounded, slowly lean your torso directly to the side toward your hanging arm, reaching that hand toward the floor.
Keeping your hips level and parallel to the floor, drive your right elbow straight back and pull the band toward your right hip.
Keeping your hips level and square to the floor, lift one leg off the ground with a controlled motion.
Keeping your hips level and square to the front, slowly raise your right (top) leg to approximately hip height.
Keeping your hips level and your spine long, begin to rotate your torso toward the side of your standing leg, reaching your arms across your body in the same direction.
Keeping your hips level and your supporting arm fully extended, lift your right hand off the seat and tap your left shoulder.
Keeping your hips level and your torso as still as possible, slowly lower your right knee until it lightly taps the floor beneath you.
Keeping your hips level and your torso from rotating, lift your right foot and tap it out to the right, roughly 12–18 inches wider.
Keeping your hips level, lift one foot slightly and tap that toe out to the side, abducting the leg.
Keeping your hips level, lift your right foot slightly and tap your toes out to the side.
Keeping your hips level, lift your right hand off the ball and tap the side of the ball firmly.
Keeping your hips level, slowly lift one hand off the floor and reach it straight forward or to your hip.
Keeping your hips low, take a small step with one hand and the opposite foot to crawl a short distance forward, staying controlled and quiet.
Keeping your hips over your knees, slowly reach one hand back to grasp the same-side heel, then the other hand to the other heel.
Keeping your hips raised and your body in that straight line, exhale and curl both heels toward your glutes by bending at the knees.
Keeping your hips raised and your glutes squeezed, slowly slide the towel toward your glutes by bending your knees — curling your heels in without letting your hips drop.

Keeping your hips square and your lower body still, exhale and slowly bend your torso directly to the right, sliding your right elbow toward your right hip.
Keeping your hips square to the floor, drive one elbow back and row the dumbbell toward your ribs.
Keeping your hips still, crunch your torso laterally by bending sideways toward your working hip, shortening the obliques on that side.
Keeping your hips up and your core braced, lower the dumbbell(s) back overhead in a controlled arc until you feel a stretch across your chest and lats.
Keeping your knee and shin still, slowly rotate your foot outward (away from the anchor) against the band's resistance.
Keeping your knee straight, lift one foot a few centimetres off the floor to take up the band slack.

Keeping your knees together and bent, slowly lower both legs to one side, stopping partway down before they reach the floor.

Keeping your legs as straight as possible, raise them in front of you by flexing at the hips until your thighs are parallel to the floor or higher.

Keeping your right leg straight, slowly raise it toward the ceiling, leading with your heel and moving only as far as your flexibility comfortably allows.

Keeping your thumbs pointing up, lift both arms off the floor by squeezing through the mid and lower back rather than shrugging your shoulders.

Keeping your working knee bent at about 90 degrees, lift that leg back and up, driving the heel toward the ceiling.

Position 1 — Hip sink: Press your hips gently downward to open the front of the left hip. Hold 2–3 seconds.
Position 2 — Thoracic rotation: Place both hands on your right thigh and rotate your torso to the right, reaching your right arm overhead toward the ceiling. Hold 2–3 seconds.
Position 3 — Side reach: Return to center and extend your left arm up and over to the right, stretching the left side of your waist. Hold 2–3 seconds.
Position 4 — Elbow drop: Lower your right elbow to the floor inside your right foot, opening the hip further. Hold 2–3 seconds.
Position 5 — Hamstring shift: Straighten your right leg and hinge your hips back with a flat back to stretch the back of the right thigh. Hold 2–3 seconds.
Position 6 — Rotation return: Rebend the right knee, rotate your torso back to center, and push through your right foot to return to standing.

Rotate your forearm upward in an arc, keeping the elbow at shoulder height, until your forearm is parallel to the floor and pointing straight ahead or slightly above horizontal.
Rotate your forearm upward so your fingers point toward the ceiling and your palm faces forward.
Rotate your forearms back in under control to the starting position, keeping the shoulder blades set.
Rotate your forearms back the other way so your palms turn rearward and down (pronation), again moving under control.
Rotate your forearms so your palms face backward (pronated grip), with the dumbbells resting just behind your thighs.
Rotate your forearms so your palms face outward — away from each other — with fingers pointing to the sides.
Rotate your forearms so your palms face up and slightly outward, setting the supinated angle that loads the inner biceps.
Rotate your hands so your palms face up and forward in a supinated, underhand grip, with the dumbbells resting against the front of your thighs.
Rotate your hands so your palms face up and toward your head — a supinated, underhand grip — with the dumbbells just outside your upper chest.
Rotate your hands to a reverse, underhand grip so your palms face toward your feet, and press the two dumbbells flat against each other.
Rotate your head to the left in the same manner, turning only as far as is comfortable.
Rotate your hips and shoulders away from the wall, loading your weight onto your back foot and coiling through your obliques.
Rotate your hips and torso to one side, lowering the kettlebell diagonally toward the outside of your opposite knee while keeping a slight bend in both knees.
Rotate your hips and torso toward the target, transferring the drive up through your core.
Rotate your hips to the left in the same controlled arc and tap the left side of the floor.
Rotate your knees back up to the neutral starting position under control.
Rotate your leg slightly inward and outward to address the full width of the muscle belly, not just the center.
Rotate your leg slightly inward and repeat the rolling motion to reach the soleus, which runs deeper and along the inner edge of the lower calf.
Rotate your palm to face the floor so your wrist is in a neutral, pronated position.
Rotate your palms back toward you and lower the dumbbells along the curl path to your sides.
Rotate your palms downward so they face the floor and confirm your elbows are still straight.
Rotate your palms to face forward and press the dumbbells overhead until your arms are fully extended and the weights stack over your shoulders.
Rotate your planted hand slightly outward (toward 10 o'clock for the left arm, 2 o'clock for the right) so your elbow tracks back and across your body during the descent.
Rotate your right arm and torso upward and to the right, reaching toward the ceiling and opening your chest.
Rotate your right arm up toward the ceiling, opening your chest and turning through your upper back — hold briefly, then return your hand to the floor.
Rotate your right elbow toward the ceiling so your fingers point forward over the foot, then gently press the foot down toward the hip without forcing it.
Rotate your right foot inward so the top of the foot or toes point slightly to the left, internally rotating the rear leg at the hip.
Rotate your right hip and shoulder toward the bag, transferring weight from your back leg onto your front leg.
Rotate your right hip and swing your right foot up and across your body toward your left hand, allowing your right hip to peel off the mat.
Rotate your shoulder externally by pressing the back of your hand upward toward the ceiling, moving only at the shoulder joint — not the elbow or wrist.
Rotate your shoulders outward (think 'armpits forward') so the stick stays stable and your chest opens toward the ceiling.
Rotate your shoulders outward to draw them away from your ears, keeping your upper arms active.
Rotate your shoulders outward to engage your upper back and pull the pipe apart slightly to create tension, keeping it directly above or just behind the crown of your head.
Rotate your thumbs toward the ceiling so your palms face each other (supinated grip).
Rotate your torso and pull the handle diagonally upward and across your body, finishing above your far shoulder.
Rotate your torso away from the machine in a smooth, controlled arc, turning through the waist while keeping your hips and head facing forward.
Rotate your torso away from the machine, pulling the handle across your body while keeping your hips and legs facing forward.
Rotate your torso away from the pulley as you pull, twisting through your obliques to finish with your chest facing forward.
Rotate your torso back through center and continue to the left, this time allowing your right arm to swing across the front and your left arm to swing behind you.
Rotate your torso back to center, keeping your hips squared and your back knee just above the floor.
Rotate your torso back to center, then drive through your heels and extend your hips and knees to stand back up to the starting position.
Rotate your torso open so your chest faces forward, not down toward the floor.
Rotate your torso slightly to the right to angle the roller toward the outer glute, or rotate left to target the inner portion near the hip.
Rotate your torso slowly to one side, turning from the waist while keeping your head and chest aligned with the bar.
Rotate your torso slowly to one side, turning from your mid-back and ribcage rather than your hips.
Rotate your torso slowly to the right, letting your shoulders roll across the ball and your arms follow, while keeping your hips level and your arms fully extended.
Rotate your torso smoothly to one side, turning from your waist while keeping your head in line with your shoulders.
Rotate your torso smoothly to one side, turning through your trunk rather than swinging your arms.
Rotate your torso so your right elbow travels toward your left knee, contracting the oblique on that side.
Rotate your torso to bring one elbow toward the opposite knee while extending the other leg out straight.
Rotate your torso to bring the opposite elbow across your body toward the raised knee until they meet or nearly touch.
Rotate your torso to bring the opposite elbow toward the bent knee, feeling the stretch through your waist and the front of the extended leg.
Rotate your torso to bring your left elbow toward your right knee while extending your left leg out straight.
Rotate your torso to bring your right elbow toward your left knee while extending your right leg out straight.
Rotate your torso to bring your right elbow toward your left knee, twisting through your waist rather than just pulling your neck.
Rotate your torso to face your left leg and repeat the reach toward your left foot.
Rotate your torso to one side under control, bringing the dumbbell toward the floor beside your hip.
Rotate your torso to one side under control, turning from the waist while your hips stay square to the front.
Rotate your torso to one side, bringing the dumbbell toward the floor next to your hip while keeping your knees tucked.
Rotate your torso to one side, lifting one arm off the floor and reaching it straight toward the ceiling so your body forms a T-shape.
Rotate your torso to one side, moving the bottle toward the floor beside your hip while your eyes and chest follow the bottle.
Rotate your torso to one side, sweeping both hands across your body in a controlled arc while keeping your arms relatively straight.
Rotate your torso to the left and throw a cross punch with your right arm, driving the rotation from your core.
Rotate your torso to the right and extend your left arm across your body in a cross punch, twisting through your obliques.
Rotate your torso to the right and raise your clasped hands up toward your right shoulder, keeping your arms relatively straight.
Rotate your torso to the right while simultaneously drawing your right knee in toward your left elbow.
Rotate your torso to the right while simultaneously driving your clasped hands down in a diagonal chopping motion toward your right hip.
Rotate your torso to the right while sweeping your clasped hands diagonally downward toward your right hip, as if chopping toward the floor.
Rotate your torso to the right, bringing the dumbbell toward the floor beside your hip while keeping your arms close to your body.
Rotate your torso to the right, bringing the kettlebell toward the floor beside your right hip. The movement comes from your waist, not your arms.
Rotate your torso to the right, bringing the medicine ball toward the floor beside your right hip.
Rotate your torso to the right, bringing the weight toward the floor beside your right hip.
Rotate your torso to the right, driving from the obliques, and lower the kettlebell until it nearly touches the floor beside your hip.
Rotate your torso to the right, lifting your right arm toward the ceiling and opening your chest to the side — hold for one to two seconds.
Rotate your torso to the right, moving the kettlebell toward the floor beside your right hip while keeping your hips square.
Rotate your torso to the right, sweeping both dumbbells up and across until your hands reach roughly shoulder height on your right side, allowing your left heel to lift naturally.
Rotate your torso toward the planted side, settling the outer thigh firmly onto the shelf created by your bent elbow.
Rotate your torso very slightly toward the pressing side to open the path, keeping your hips square and your non-pressing arm relaxed at your side.
Rotate your trunk away from the anchor, pulling the band diagonally up and across your body toward the opposite shoulder.
Rotate your trunk to one side and bring the rope across your body toward the floor beside your hip.
Rotate your upper body to one side, reaching the arm on that side upward while your lower body remains still and your squat position holds.

Rotate your wrist and 'thread' your hand under the bell so that the bell flips around your forearm and settles in the rack position: bell resting on your forearm, elbow pointed forward and down, upper arm close to your chest at shoulder height.
Rotate your wrist so your palm faces down (pronated), letting the loaded end of the dumbbell drop toward the floor.
Rotate your wrist so your palm faces downward (pronation) — this is your starting position.
Rotate your wrist so your palm faces your shoulder as you lift, squeezing the biceps hard at the top.
Rotate your wrists back to the pronated, overhand position as you begin to lower.
Rotate your wrists in the opposite direction to turn the dumbbells outward, again to a comfortable end range.
Rotate your wrists so your palms face back toward your thighs, holding the dumbbells with a pronated (overhand) grip.
Rotate your wrists so your palms face each other and press the inner heads of the dumbbells together, keeping them in firm contact.
Rotate your wrists so your palms face forward (supinated grip) and let your hands turn slightly outward, away from your body.
Rotate your wrists so your palms face forward and bring the dumbbells to shoulder level, ready to press.
Rotate your wrists so your thumbs point slightly downward, as if pouring out a jug, to bias the side of the shoulder.
Round your spine into a C-curve: tuck your chin gently toward your chest, hollow your lower belly, and tilt your pelvis slightly backward so your tailbone points toward the floor.
Round your upper back and push your hands forward, drawing your shoulder blades wide apart.
Round your upper back and tuck your chin toward your chest to take tension off your lower-back erectors and bias the glutes.
Round your upper back by drawing your shoulder blades apart and allowing your chest to cave inward slightly — think of making a C-shape with your spine from shoulders to mid-back.
Round your upper back by pushing your hands forward and allowing your shoulder blades to separate as wide as possible.
Round your upper back slightly and tuck your chin toward your chest — this posture takes the lower back out of the movement and shifts the load to the glutes.
Round your upper back slightly, allowing the stretch to travel through the thoracic spine and into the lower back.
Row again as you land, completing one rep on each side. Continue alternating legs and rowing for the prescribed time or rep count, keeping a steady rhythm throughout.
Row both dumbbells toward your lower ribs by driving your elbows up and back, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Row both dumbbells up toward the sides of your ribcage, driving your elbows up and back rather than flaring them out.
Row both hands back toward your lower ribs, leading with your elbows and keeping them close to your sides.
Row one dumbbell to your ribs by driving the elbow up and back, keeping it close to your body while the opposite arm presses the floor.
Row one dumbbell up toward your hip, driving your elbow back and keeping it close to your ribs while your hips and shoulders stay level.
Row one kettlebell toward your hip by driving your elbow back and up, keeping it close to your torso. At the top, briefly retract and depress the scapula on that side.
Row one kettlebell toward your hip by driving your elbow straight back, keeping it close to your torso.
Row the band toward your lower ribs by driving your elbows back close to your sides, keeping your wrists straight.
Row the band toward your upper abdomen and lower chest, driving your elbows out and back at roughly a 45-degree angle from your torso.
Row the bar straight up toward the underside of the bench, driving your elbows up and back until the bar nearly touches the bench.
Row the bar toward your lower ribs or upper stomach, driving your elbows back and up against the band's tension.
Row the bar toward your upper chest, flaring your elbows out to roughly 90° from your torso to emphasize the rear delts.
Row the bar up toward the underside of the bench by driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Row the bar up toward the underside of the bench by driving your elbows out and back at roughly a 45–60° angle from your torso.
Row the bar up toward your lower chest, driving your elbows back and down close to your sides.
Row the dumbbell up toward your hip and lower ribs, driving your elbow back and close to your side rather than flaring it out.
Row the dumbbell up toward your hip by driving your elbow back and squeezing your back, keeping it close to your side.
Row the dumbbells until they reach the sides of your torso and your shoulder blades are fully squeezed together.
Row the dumbbells up and out to the sides, leading with your elbows and keeping them flared at roughly 90° to your torso.
Row the dumbbells up and out toward the sides of your ribcage, leading with your elbows as they travel wide away from your torso.
Row the handle back toward your hip, leading with your elbow and driving it past your torso.
Row the handle up until your elbow passes your torso and you feel a firm contraction in your lat and mid-back.
Row the handles toward your lower abdomen, keeping your elbows close to your sides and driving them straight back rather than flaring them out.
Row the kettlebells upward until your upper arms are parallel to the floor and your elbows are at shoulder height.
Row the opposite dumbbell with the same control, then return to the start to complete one rep.
Row the right dumbbell to the side of your ribs, driving your elbow up while keeping your hips level and resisting any rotation.
Row the right kettlebell up toward your hip by driving your elbow back and simultaneously rotating your right shoulder slightly upward.
Row until the stick reaches roughly chest or lower-chin height, feeling the contraction in the side of your shoulder.
Row your chest up to the bar, driving your elbows back and keeping them at roughly a 45-degree angle from your torso.
Row your chest up toward the handles until your hands reach the sides of your torso, squeezing your shoulder blades together at the top.
Row your chest up until it nearly touches the bar, keeping your body rigid and your elbows tracking at roughly 45 degrees from your torso.
Run at full effort for the designated distance (typically 20–100 meters), maintaining an upright but slightly forward-leaning torso.
Run in place or over a short distance for 3–5 quick steps, pumping your arms naturally.
Scan for a tender or tight spot by making small, deliberate shifts of body weight — forward, back, or slightly side-to-side — until you locate a point of significant tension.
Scan from your feet to your head, consciously releasing any area still holding tension.
Scoop your chest forward and down in a smooth arc, keeping your hips lower than at the start as your body sweeps through the bottom position.
Scoot your hips as close to the wall as is comfortable, or allow a small gap if that feels better for your lower back.
Second pull: as the bar reaches your upper thighs, violently extend your hips, knees and ankles (triple extension), shrugging and staying tall.

Secure a resistance band to a stable anchor point directly above you — a pull-up bar or a sturdy rack works well. Lie on your back below the anchor with your arms extended overhead gripping the band or another fixed support for stability.
Secure an ankle weight around the ankle of your working leg, or hook a light weight plate over the top of your foot as an alternative load.
Secure one end of a barbell in a landmine attachment or a corner, and load the opposite end with the desired weight.
Secure one end of a barbell in a landmine attachment or wedge it firmly into a corner protected by a weight plate.
Secure the cuff around the ankle of your outside (working) leg, then stand side-on to the machine so the cable crosses in front of your standing leg.
Secure your feet under a fixed support so your heels stay locked down throughout the movement.
Secure your lower body against the hip pads or thigh supports so your hips and legs remain fixed throughout the movement.
Secure your working leg between the ankle pads and let the other leg hang free or rest off to the side, keeping it out of the way.
Select a dumbbell of appropriate weight and place it near the captain's chair before you mount the station.

Select a dumbbell or weight plate you can control through a full range of motion. Sit on the stability ball and rest the weight on your thighs, holding it with both hands — grip the top plate of a dumbbell or the inner rim of a weight plate.
Select a light weight plate and lie on your side on a flat bench so your head extends just off the end, with your ear parallel to the floor and your body in a straight line from head to toe.
Select a light-to-moderate weight to begin, especially if this is your first time on the machine.
Select a lighter kettlebell than you would normally press; the bottoms-up position significantly increases the stability demand.
Select a very light weight plate to start — even experienced lifters should begin with 2.5–5 lb until the movement pattern is well established.
Select a weight plate or dumbbell and sit on the center of a stability ball, feet flat on the floor about hip-width apart.
Select an appropriate weight on the leverage machine and adjust the seat height so your hips are level with or slightly above the machine's pivot point.
Select an appropriately light plate load — the neck responds well to low weight and high control.
Select the appropriate resistance on the machine and attach or position the single-arm neutral-grip handle.
Select your desired weight on the stack and adjust the seat height so the handles are level with the middle of your chest.

Select your load — a weight plate held against your chest, a dumbbell cradled at the chest, or a barbell across the upper back for heavier sessions. If using a plate or dumbbell, hold it firmly with both hands before mounting.
Select your target resistance level on the leverage machine — start light to warm up, then increase to a level where you can sustain a cadence of 70–100 RPM.
Select your weight on the weight stack and position yourself against the pad, feet flat on the floor or platform.
Separate your hands as you pull, drawing the rope ends past your ears until your hands are level with your forehead.
Set a bar at about chest height — a power-rack pin, Smith bar, or low fixed bar works.
Set a bar at approximately waist height when seated — a Smith machine, barbell in a rack, or sturdy low bar all work.
Set a bar at roughly chest-to-head height — low enough that you can reach it with your feet still on the floor.
Set a bar at roughly chest-to-hip height in a rack or use a low fixed bar so your feet can stay on the floor when your arms are extended.
Set a bar at roughly waist to hip height in a squat rack, Smith machine, or on sturdy parallettes. Sit on the floor directly underneath it.
Set a bar in a rack or Smith machine at roughly hip height — lower means more horizontal body angle and greater difficulty.
Set a bar in a rack or use a sturdy horizontal surface at roughly hip height.
Set a bar in a rack, Smith machine, or use a sturdy table at roughly hip height — the lower the bar, the harder the exercise.
Set a barbell across your upper back (not your neck), resting it on your traps and gripping it slightly wider than shoulder-width. Unrack it and step back into an open space.
Set a barbell across your upper back (on the traps, not the neck) and grip it with both hands wider than shoulder-width, just as you would for a squat.
Set a barbell across your upper back and unrack it, resting the bar on your traps with your hands gripping it just outside your shoulders.
Set a barbell across your upper back, resting it on your traps and shoulders as you would for a back squat, and grip it firmly with both hands.
Set a barbell across your upper back, resting it on your traps and shoulders, and grip it firmly outside shoulder-width.
Set a barbell across your upper back, resting it on your traps and shoulders, and grip it slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Set a barbell across your upper back, resting it on your traps rather than your neck, and grip it slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Set a barbell at shoulder height in a rack, or clean and press it overhead, taking a grip slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Set a barbell at shoulder height in a rack, or clean it up to your shoulders, and rest it across the front of your shoulders in the front-rack position with your elbows high and pointing forward.
Set a barbell at upper-chest height in a rack and position the bar across your upper back (traps), gripping it slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Set a barbell in a landmine attachment (or wedge one end into a corner). Position a flat bench parallel to the barbell, close enough that you can brace your non-working hand or forearm on it.
Set a barbell in a landmine sleeve or wedge one end into a corner. Load the free end with an appropriate weight.
Set a barbell in a rack at about lower-chest height and step under it so the bar rests in the crooks of your elbows.
Set a barbell in a rack at about shoulder height, or clean and press it overhead to start.
Set a barbell in a rack at about shoulder height, or clean it from the floor to your shoulders. Grip it slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Set a barbell in a rack at about upper-chest height, step under it, and rest it across your upper back (not your neck) with a grip slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Set a barbell in a rack at upper-chest height and grip it just outside shoulder-width.
Set a barbell in a rack at upper-chest height and load it light — this is an activation drill, not a max lift.
Set a barbell in a rack at upper-chest height and load it. Step under the bar so it rests across your upper traps, not your neck.
Set a barbell in a rack at upper-chest height and place a low plate or wedge where your heels will sit.
Set a barbell in a rack at upper-chest height and position a sturdy bench at a comfortable knee-to-hip height to one side.
Set a barbell in a rack at upper-chest height, step under it, and rest it across your upper back (traps), not your neck.
Set a barbell in a rack at upper-chest height. Take a front-rack grip with your hands just outside shoulder-width and your elbows driven high so the bar rests across the front of your shoulders.
Set a barbell in a rack or Smith machine at roughly hip height — the bar should be low enough that your arms are fully extended when you hang beneath it.
Set a barbell in a rack, or find a fixed bar, at roughly hip height — the lower the bar, the more of your bodyweight you will press.
Set a barbell on a rack at about thigh height, or deadlift it into position from the floor.
Set a barbell on a rack at shoulder height and unrack it onto your upper traps, gripping it just wider than shoulder-width.
Set a barbell or fixed bar in a power rack so it rests at mid-thigh height — roughly at the junction of your upper and lower thigh when you stand tall.
Set a bench or box behind you at a height that puts your hip crease at or just below knee level when seated, and load the barbell in a rack at upper-chest height.
Set a bench or box behind you at a height that puts your hips roughly level with your knees at the bottom, and position a loaded barbell in the rack.
Set a bench or sturdy platform about knee height behind you and rest the barbell in a rack at lower-chest level.
Set a bench to a moderate decline and lie back so your head is below your hips, securing your feet under the foot pads or roller.
Set a bench to a slight decline and lie face down on it so your knees clear the lower edge and your hips stay supported.
Set a bench to a slight-to-moderate decline and secure your legs under the pads or rollers.
Set a Bosu ball flat-side down in front of you and hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides with arms straight.
Set a box or bench behind you at a height that puts your hips at or just below parallel when seated. Stand facing away from it with feet shoulder-width apart and toes turned out slightly.
Set a box or bench behind you at a height that puts your hips roughly level with or just above your knees when seated.
Set a cable machine to its lowest pulley position and attach a straight bar, rope, or single handle. Load an appropriate weight on the stack.
Set a cable pulley to a high anchor point and attach a single handle.
Set a cable pulley to a high position and attach a rope or straight bar handle.
Set a cable pulley to about chest height and attach a single handle. Stand side-on to the machine so the working arm is the one farthest from the stack.
Set a cable pulley to about elbow height and attach a single handle.
Set a cable pulley to about waist height and attach a handle. Stand side-on to the machine and hold the handle in both hands at your chest, stepping out so the cable is under light tension.
Set a cable pulley to chest height and attach a single handle. Lie on your back on the floor (or a bench) so the cable line runs across your body, perpendicular to your spine.

Set a cable pulley to its highest position and attach a single handle. Stand to the side of the machine so the cable runs diagonally across your body, and grasp the handle with the hand closest to the stack.
Set a cable pulley to its lowest position and attach a single handle.
Set a cable pulley to its lowest position and attach a single handle. Place a flat bench alongside the machine.
Set a cable pulley to its lowest position and attach a straight or EZ bar, then place a preacher bench a step in front of the machine facing away from it.
Set a cable pulley to its lowest position and fasten an ankle strap around your working ankle.
Set a cable pulley to roughly chest height and attach a single handle.
Set a cable pulley to roughly chest height and attach a single handle. Stand side-on to the machine and grip the handle with both hands.
Set a cable pulley to roughly chest height and attach a single-grip handle.
Set a cable pulley to roughly chest or shoulder height and attach a single-handle grip.
Set a cable pulley to roughly elbow height and attach a single D-handle.
Set a cable pulley to roughly head height and attach a single handle.
Set a cable pulley to roughly shoulder height and attach a single handle.
Set a cable pulley to roughly shoulder height and select a light, controllable weight.
Set a cable pulley to roughly shoulder height or slightly above, and attach a single D-handle.
Set a cable pulley to roughly upper-chest height and attach a rope or dual handles.
Set a cable pulley to roughly waist height and attach a belt or single handle. Step into the belt or hold the handle at your midline and back away until the cable is taut.
Set a cable pulley to the lowest position and attach a single D-handle.
Set a cable pulley to the lowest position and attach a single handle. Sit on a bench placed in front of the stack.
Set a cable pulley to the lowest position and attach a straight or EZ bar; place a flat bench in front of the stack so its head end points toward the pulley.
Set a cable pulley to the lowest position and attach an ankle cuff. Fasten the cuff securely around the ankle of your working leg.
Set a cable pulley to the lowest position and attach an ankle strap, then fasten the strap around the ankle of the working leg.
Set a clear front reference point on the floor and keep your chest up with arms relaxed and ready to drive.
Set a close grip, hands roughly shoulder-width or slightly inside, wrapping your thumbs fully around the bar so it sits over the base of your palms.
Set a decline bench and lie face-down (prone) on the pad with your chest supported and your head past the top edge so it can move freely.
Set a decline bench to a moderate angle and hook your feet securely under the foot pads or roller at the high end.
Set a decline bench to a moderate angle and lie back along it with your head at the high end.
Set a decline bench to a moderate angle and lock your feet under the foot pads or roller.
Set a decline bench to a moderate angle and secure your feet under the ankle pads or footrest at the top.
Set a decline bench to your desired angle, typically between 30 and 45 degrees, and secure your feet under the foot pads.
Set a dual cable pulley (or two low pulleys) to the lowest position and attach a single handle to each side.
Set a dumbbell of equal weight on the floor on each side of your feet, standing midway between them.
Set a dumbbell on the floor beside a flat bench. Place your near knee and same-side hand on the bench so your torso is roughly parallel to the floor.
Set a dumbbell on the floor beside a power rack upright. Stand to the side and grip the upright at roughly waist height with your non-working hand.
Set a dumbbell on the floor beside one foot. Stand tall with your feet about hip-width apart.
Set a dumbbell on the floor between your feet, stand with feet about hip-width apart, and grip the handle with one hand using a neutral grip.
Set a dumbbell on the floor outside each foot and stand with your feet about hip-width apart, dumbbells resting at your sides.
Set a fixed bar (pull-up bar, Smith machine bar, or rack bar) at approximately chest to shoulder height.
Set a fixed bar at roughly hip-to-chest height in a squat rack or on a Smith machine, and check that it is locked and stable.
Set a fixed bar, railing, or rack pin at roughly chest-to-waist height and confirm it is stable and will not move.
Set a flat bench across the safety arms of a power rack, high enough that the dumbbells hang clear of the floor at full stretch.
Set a flat bench and grab a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip (palms facing each other).
Set a flat bench and grab a single dumbbell. Lie back on the bench with your head supported and your feet planted firmly on the floor.
Set a flat bench behind you and load the barbell on a rack at upper-chest height.
Set a flat bench behind you and load the barbell, then step under it and rack the bar across the front of your shoulders, fingertips under the bar with your elbows lifted high.
Set a flat bench behind you and place a sturdy plate or low platform on the floor in front of it for your front foot to stand on.
Set a flat bench behind you and stand just in front of it with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes turned slightly out.
Set a flat bench beside you and stand alongside it with your feet about shoulder-width apart and toes turned slightly out.
Set a flat bench in front of a low cable pulley and attach a straight or short bar. Sit at the end of the bench facing away from the machine.
Set a flat bench inside a rack, high enough that a loaded barbell can hang at arm's length below it without touching the floor.
Set a flat bench inside the rack and rest a loaded barbell on safety pins or J-hooks just below bench height, so you can reach it from a face-down position.
Set a flat bench inside the rack, elevated so the loaded barbell can hang at full arm's length below it. Position the bar on the floor or low safeties directly beneath the bench.
Set a flat bench inside the Smith machine and position it so the bar, when lowered, will rest across the lower portion of your thighs, just above your knees.
Set a flat bench lengthwise and load a barbell on the floor at the foot end. Lie face-down on the bench so your hips are near the end and your torso is fully supported.
Set a flat bench on or inside a power rack at a height that lets the loaded barbell hang at full arm length without the plates touching the floor.
Set a flat bench or box behind you at a height that puts your hip crease at or slightly below your knees when seated. Place a loaded barbell in a rack at upper-chest height.
Set a flat or low bench inside a Smith machine and position it directly behind you so it will contact the back of your thighs at the bottom of a full squat.
Set a handle on each high pulley and select a light-to-moderate weight on both stacks.
Set a handle on the low pulley of each side of a cable station, or work one low pulley at a time, and select a light-to-moderate weight.
Set a heavy dumbbell on the floor beside a flat bench or rack. Plant the same-side foot back and place your free hand firmly on the bench for support.
Set a high cable pulley above shoulder height and attach a single-handle grip.
Set a horizontal bar at roughly hip height when you are seated on the floor. Sit directly beneath the bar with your legs extended straight out in front of you.

Set a hyperextension bench (Roman chair) to the 45-degree position. Stand next to it and place the side of your hip against the large pad, positioning it just below your hip bone so your torso can move freely.

WRONG — intentionally round your lower and upper back, letting your chest cave forward and your tailbone tuck under as you begin to descend. Hold this position briefly so you can feel the spinal flexion and forward knee collapse it produces.
WRONG — Let your hips sag toward the floor so your body forms a downward curve. Notice how this collapses the waist and removes tension from the lateral core. This is the position to avoid.
WRONG — Pike: Deliberately raise your hips toward the ceiling until your body forms an inverted V. Hold for a moment and notice how tension shifts off your core and onto your shoulders.
WRONG — Sag: Lower your hips until they drop toward the floor. Hold briefly and notice the excessive arch in your lower back and the loss of abdominal tension.
WRONG (alternative) — Raise your hips too high so your body forms an inverted V (piked). This also misaligns the spine and shifts load away from the target area.
WRONG: Raise the dumbbells overhead or past shoulder height, and turn your palms to face upward (like pouring water), which shifts tension away from the side delts.
WRONG: Shrug your shoulders upward and swing the dumbbells up using momentum, allowing your torso to lean back and your elbows to drop below your wrists at the top.
